claims.claim: At temperature 0, an LLM produced 80 unique completions over 1000 runs, and with batch-invariant kernels all 1000 were identical; the cause is that load, and thus batch size, varies nondeterministically.
claims.reason: Excerpt states 1000 completions identical with batch-invariant kernels vs 80 unique unoptimized at temp 0, and that load/batch-size nondeterministically varies.

claims.claim: Batch-invariant kernels cost roughly 2x (55 seconds versus 26 seconds), narrowing to 1.6x with improved attention kernels (42 seconds).
claims.reason: Excerpt gives ~2x slower (55s vs 26s) reducing to 1.6x with improved attention kernels (42s).

claims.claim: LLM-42 decodes with a non-deterministic fast path and enforces determinism via a lightweight verify-rollback loop, reusing existing kernels and incurring overhead only in proportion to the traffic that requires determinism.
claims.reason: Excerpt matches: non-deterministic fast path, lightweight verify-rollback loop, re-uses existing kernels, overhead only proportional to traffic requiring determinism.
